Live Lightly is designed to catalyse a low carbon lifestyle movement among Aucklanders. It encourages sustainable lifestyle choices across 6 climate action themes including energy, transport, diet, consumer behaviour, biodiversity and communications. Specifically, the themes are: Power, Move, Eat, Shop, Grow and Talk. To support delivery of this programme, a consumption emissions model that takes a top-down approach to calculating household consumption emissions based on household income and expenditure, has been designed. The model has an interface called 'FutureFit', a gamified online tool (https://www.futurefit.nz) designed for use by the public, councils and corporate entities. FutureFit has been developed with the specific objective of empowering users to quantify their carbon footprint, and then challenges users to reduce their footprint through a range of actions. (2) Auckland Council's Sustainable Schools programme. It supports schools to quantify and reduce their carbon footprint. (3) Transport Emissions Reduction Pathway (TERP). TERP was endorsed by Auckland Transport's board and adopted by Auckland Council in August 2022. The TERP gives effect to Te Tāruke-ā-Tāwhiri's (Auckland's Climate Plan) target to halve Auckland's regional emissions by 2030 (against a 2016 baseline). It sets out: * what needs to happen to reduce Auckland's transport emissions by 64 per cent by 2030 * what it will look like when we get there * to identify the potential barriers to achieving it. The TERP provides formal direction that Auckland Council and Auckland Transport must follow in all of their activities. (4) More Aucklanders are using public transport to get around. The Second Daegu Metropolitan City Resource Recycling Implementation Plan focuses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions by promoting waste reduction and resource circulation. Key strategies include:

Strengthening Resource Circulation: Shift from petroleum-based plastics to bio-plastics by 2050 and improve collection and sorting systems for high-quality recycled materials.

Promoting Eco-friendly Consumption: Expand refill stores, standardize reusable containers, and encourage reusable container delivery, with support through online platforms.

Expanding Waste Recycling: Increase pyrolysis processing of plastics and bio-gasification of food waste, and simplify criteria for recognizing recyclable resources.

Establishing a Stable Processing System: Implement import cooperation fees to fund facility improvements and support local residents.

Transitioning to a Circular Economy: Enhance system efficiency and create legal frameworks to support resource recycling across production, distribution, and consumption stages.

Goyang City, a representative urban-rural complex, has established an ordinance to promote local food production and consumption. Through this ordinance, Goyang City aims to reduce its carbon footprint by promoting local food consumption.

2. Goyang City Local Food Plan (2023-2027)
- Background and Purpose:
The plan was established under the Goyang City Basic Ordinance on Food Security (Article 5), which mandates a five-year local food plan. Its purpose is to build a sustainable food system that responds to climate-induced “food shocks” by creating a circular economy encompassing production, distribution, processing, consumption, entrepreneurship, waste management, and resource recycling.

- Vision: A city where all citizens enjoy safe and healthy food.

- Strategic Objectives
a. Eco-friendly food circulation system - reducing carbon emissions across the food cycle from production to waste.

b. Expansion of local food in public catering - ensuring access to safe and fresh local produce through schools, public meals, and direct sales markets.

c. Revitalization of the food economy - fostering food-related social enterprises, community groups, and start-ups.

d. Strengthening governance and policy foundation - establishing integrated food support centers, monitoring systems, and participatory governance.

- Key Targets (by 2026 / 2030)
Eco-friendly certified farmland: 240ha → 340ha
Certified eco-friendly farms: 250 → 350
Local food direct stores: 19 → 25
Food community groups: 50 → 100
Food-related jobs & start-ups: 550 → 1,100
Local food ambassadors (“Local Alimi”): 500 → 900
Food council operations: 20 → 36 meetings annually

- Implementation Phases
2020-2023: Preparatory phase (ordinance enactment, food council, pilot projects).
2024-2025: Establishment of integrated food policy system (Food Support Center, DB system).
2026-2027: Stabilization and expansion (new initiatives, scaling up best practices)

- Budget & Investment
Estimated total: ₩12.6 billion (approx. $9.5 million) over five years.
Funding sources: National, provincial, and municipal budgets, plus private cooperation

- Representative Programs
“Local Food Carbon Diet Project” (carbon points for eco-friendly consumption).
Local food meal kits & recipe development.
Special crop branding (e.g., Ilsan Yeolmu radish, Gawaji rice).
Food sharing initiatives (community kitchens, food banks, shared refrigerators).
Youth and community engagement in food-related jobs and social enterprises

In short:
The plan is Goyang City's five-year roadmap to create a sustainable, resilient, and inclusive food system. It emphasizes climate response, local economy revitalization, and citizen participation, aiming to secure food safety and health for all residents.

Goyang City Green Building Design Standards (2021- )

(Public Notice No. 2021-1250)

Purpose
To establish detailed design standards that reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the building sector and promote sustainable, eco-friendly architecture in Goyang City. The standards serve as the city's action plan for implementing national green building and carbon neutrality policies at the local level.

Scope of Application

Applies to newly constructed, extended, or renovated buildings within Goyang City.

Mandatory for public buildings; recommended/expanded for private developments.

Key Strategies for GHG Reduction in Buildings

Energy Performance and Efficiency

Compliance with high energy efficiency grades (Building Energy Efficiency Rating System).

Installation of high-performance insulation, windows, and materials to minimize heating/cooling loads.

Introduction of Zero-Energy Building (ZEB) standards in stages.

Use of Renewable and Low-Carbon Energy

Mandatory installation of renewable energy systems (e.g., solar PV, geothermal, fuel cells) above a set capacity threshold.

Encouragement of all-electric and hydrogen-based energy systems to replace fossil fuels.

Eco-Friendly Building Materials

Prioritization of low-carbon, recycled, and certified green materials.

Restrictions on high-carbon construction materials and promotion of resource-efficient design.

Water and Waste Management

Application of water-saving devices and rainwater harvesting.

Design standards for on-site waste separation and recycling spaces.

Indoor Environmental Quality

Mandatory natural ventilation, daylight access, and eco-friendly interior materials.

Indoor air quality standards (formaldehyde, VOC limits).

Smart and Integrated Design

Expansion of Building Energy Management Systems (BEMS).

Smart meters and IoT-based monitoring to optimize energy use.

Institutional Mechanisms

Mandatory Green Building Certification for public projects.

Incentives (e.g., floor area ratio bonuses, financial support) for private developers adopting advanced green standards.

Regular monitoring and public disclosure of building energy/GHG performance.

Expected Outcomes

Progressive reduction of building-sector greenhouse gas emissions, contributing to Goyang's 2030 (-36%) and 2034 (-39%) GHG reduction targets.

Increased number of zero-energy and low-carbon buildings in both public and private sectors.

Establishment of Goyang as a leading eco-friendly city aligned with Korea's Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Act.

✅ In short:
Goyang's building-sector GHG reduction plan centers on zero-energy building standards, renewable energy integration, eco-friendly materials, water/waste efficiency, and smart energy management. It is designed to make green construction the norm, not the exception, and directly supports the city's carbon neutrality roadmap.

Goyang City Resource Circulation Execution Plan (2023-2027)

Background and Purpose
This plan was formulated under the Framework Act on Resource Circulation and relevant national/provincial strategies. It aims to shift from waste treatment to a circular economy model, emphasizing waste reduction at source, resource recovery, and sustainable urban management .

Vision
A sustainable circular economy city that minimizes waste, maximizes recycling, and improves citizens' quality of life.

Strategic Directions

Waste reduction at source - promoting eco-friendly consumption, reducing disposable items, and industrial waste prevention.

Strengthening recycling infrastructure - upgrading public recycling facilities, supporting construction waste reuse, and expanding food waste bioenergy conversion.

Safe and efficient treatment - modernizing incineration, landfill, and hazardous waste facilities, while minimizing environmental risks.

Governance and participation - fostering citizen engagement, public-private partnerships, and transparent monitoring systems

Governance model: operation of Resource Circulation Council with annual evaluation .

El Plan de Movilidad y Espacio Público de VG recoge el desarrollo de zonas de bajas emisiones (ZEB) como uno de los pilares fundamentales de la nueva movilidad urbana, señalando que se parte de la experiencia previa de la implantación de la Zona de Tráfico Limitado (ZTL) implantada hace unos años en el marco de la participación en el proyecto CIVITAS MODERN.
La implantación de la ZBE en Vitoria-Gasteiz se hará en tres fases, de forma gradual y consensuada. El perímetro marcado para la primera fase de implantación corresponde a la zona del Casco Medieval y parte del Ensanche. Conllevará las siguientes medidas: eliminar el tráfico de paso, instalar cámaras para lectura de matrículas y establecer permisos de acceso puntual. La intervención tiene un presupuesto inicial de 727.437,48 euros. El sistema de control de accesos que se va a instalar dará cobertura tanto a la fase 1 como a la fase 2 de la ZEB. La fase 1, cuya vigencia está prevista hasta 2027, abarcará el Casco Medieval y la parte del Ensanche delimitada por las calles La Paz, Ortiz de Zárate, Florida, Ramón y Cajal, Luis Heintz, Magdalena, Vicente Goicoechea y Cercas Bajas. En todos los accesos a este perímetro se instalarán 22 cámaras. Las cámaras incorporarán una doble óptica: una para lectura de matrículas y otra para observación del contexto de tráfico. Con ello se pretende que todo el sistema, más allá de la regulación de accesos, permita también labores de análisis de tráfico, reparto modal y otros conceptos para la optimización de futuras actuaciones y medidas a implantar.
Igualmente, se dejarán instaladas las 8 cámaras necesarias para controlar en un futuro la fase 2 de la ZEB, prevista para 2027, que tendrá tres cambios sustanciales: modificación del perímetro de restricción de tráfico (ampliado por las calles Ramiro de Maeztu, Domingo Beltrán y Coronación), establecimiento de restricciones según distintivo ambiental y activación de la OTA ambiental.
En 2030 llegará la tercera fase de la ZEB, donde se prevé un mayor grado de restricción de paso de vehículos en base a sus distintivos ambientales y una nueva ampliación del ámbito de la OTA ambiental.
Entre los meses de noviembre-diciembre de 2023 se ha llevado a cabo el proceso participativo para definir el modo de funcionamiento del tráfico en la ZBE. Igualmente, se trabaja en la redacción de la ordenanza específica que regulará este mismo aspecto. También se está definiendo la campaña informativa que precederá al inicio de la restricción del paso.
La implantación de la ZEB está financiada con fondos europeos Next Generation en el marco del Plan de Recuperación, Transformación y Resiliencia del Estado español.

column16: Konpondu es un proyecto del Ayuntamiento de Vitoria-Gasteiz que busca promover un cambio en el modelo de consumo actual de la ciudadanía con el objetivo de prolongar la vida útil de los productos a través del sector local de la reparación. Konpondu se materializa en un Buscador de comercios de reparación dentro de la web municipal, donde es posible encontrar profesionales de la reparación de productos de consumo que van desde gran y pequeño electrodoméstico hasta ropa y calzado, pasando por equipos de imagen y sonido, muebles, etc. así como información y documentación relacionada con la reparación y la economía circular. Los objetivo s del proyecto son: promover un modelo de consumo que se aleje del usar y tirar, que amplíe la duración de la vida de las cosas. De esa forma, se consigue reducir la presión sobre los recursos del Planeta y la generación de residuos; reflexionar sobre nuestro modelo de consumo y sobre los productos que compramos y de la importancia de ser selectivos a la hora de adquirirlos, eligiendo aquellos que sean más duraderos y reparables; poner en valor el sector local de la reparación, que genera empleo cualificado y no deslocalizable y que es un aliado contra la obsolescencia programada y percibida y un agente clave en una estrategia local de economía circular. La persona que es Konponder no es únicamente aquella que apuesta por reparar antes que tirar; también es Konponder la persona, el o la profesional, que se dedica a la reparación. En un escenario de crisis climática, de contaminación de los océanos y de escasez de materias primas, la utilización de servicios de reparación se presenta no solo como un tipo de consumo responsable, sino también como un consumo transformador del planeta y de la economía. En un contexto de crisis planetaria de materias primas nace el proyecto Konpondu, que se materializa en un Buscador de comercios de reparación. Se puede obtener más información en el siguiente enlace: https://www.vitoria-gasteiz.org/wb021/was/contenidoAction.do?idioma=es&uid=u50993cf2_1781a8edc14__7fb6

La Estrategia de Circularidad de Vitoria-Gasteiz 2030, aspira a que Vitoria-Gasteiz se convierta en un territorio resiliente que garantiza el bienestar de la ciudadanía en un contexto de contracción material; contribuye a los retos globales de la neutralidad climática y de la preservación de la biodiversidad, mediante un tejido económico local innovador basado en la retención del valor de los materiales durante el mayor tiempo posible y ajustado a los límites biofísicos del planeta.
Se han definido cinco objetivos estratégicos: 1) Reducir el consumo de materias primas del sistema VG, 2) Aumentar la productividad material, 3) Aumentar la tasa de uso de material circular (mercado de materias primas secundarias, reutilización y PxR), 4) Reducir la tasa de generación de residuos y 5) Aumentar el bienestar de la ciudadanía, a partir de los cuales se han establecido un conjunto de acciones a llevar a cabo en los próximos años.
La mayor parte de las acciones planificadas contribuyen, a la reducción de emisiones de GEI de nuestro territorio, así como al aumento de su resiliencia.

The Orgânico project (https://organico.portoambiente.pt/) : implements an intelligent food waste collection system with access-controlled street containers, currently covering 60% of the city to improve the quality of collected organic waste.
Vegetable Gardens: aims to establish a network of local entities to promote home composting, organic farming, and kitchen gardens in Greater Porto, with 13 operational gardens serving 527 users in 2024.
Home and Community Composting (LIPOR): launched in 2007, helps Porto residents recycle food and garden waste at home, reducing costs and CO2 emissions while improving soil and plant quality through organic compost use. By 2024, it had distributed 2500 composters, diverting around 958.73 tons of biowaste annually, and supported two community composting areas with 133 families that prevented the collection and transport of 6.8 tons of food waste.
Dose Certa (LIPOR): partnering with the Portuguese Association of Nutrition, works with catering establishments to reduce food waste and costs through tailored improvement plans, resulting in 1 ton of food waste avoided across 36 participants from 2012 to 2024.
EMBRULHA (LIPOR): started in 2016, provides participating restaurants with free biodegradable packaging to help customers take leftovers home, preventing 5.5 tons of food waste per year across 61 restaurants by 2024.
Fruta Feia (https://frutafeia.pt): Fruta Feia aims to reduce food waste by rescuing good-quality 'ugly' produce returned by farmers, raising awareness about food waste, and providing affordable local food, preventing nearly 114 tons of waste in 2023.
Zero Waste: The Zero Desperdício initiative, supported by LIPOR and Porto Municipality, emerged from a citizens' movement to recover food waste for consumption, animal feed, or composting, avoiding 781 tons of food waste and providing 1561.571 meals worth €3903.927 between 2019 and August 2025.
Good Food Hubs (https://goodfoodhubs.pt/): aims to promote healthy, sustainable, and local food in Porto by connecting local producers and consumers through itinerant markets, digital platforms, and food-related events, with its pilot phase focused on the Asprela area—a major university and healthcare hub. Between October 2022 and December 2023, the project held 64 markets with 11 producers, reaching 2,426 customers, transacting over 3006 kg of organic food worth €11737, and avoiding 355 kg CO2 eq., contributing to a more sustainable and localized food system.
Sustainable food model: A sustainable food model is being created in canteens, namely through the introduction of additional criteria (organic, local, and seasonal products) in the contracting of services for municipal canteens, which serve schools and employees.

column16: The Municipality developed the \'Environmental Index\' to motivate recovery, rehabilitation, and construction companies to adopt natural-based solutions in their projects. The document is under public revision and has the dual objective of improving the bioclimatic comfort of the city's buildings and reducing the vulnerability of the most fragile ones to extreme climatic episodes. At the same time, the index will contribute to the decarbonisation of the city. The benefits include reduced licensing fees and increased construction rates in certain areas of the city for those who exceed the legal requirements for energy efficiency and permeability. Additionally, those who adopt more sustainable solutions in water management, green infrastructure, building materials and waste management will also benefit.

column16: ReBOOT was a computer recovery, repair and sharing project with the dual objectives of reducing expenditure and conserving natural resources, while also facilitating the transfer of knowledge. The project was promoted by the Municipality and has the support of other local and national entities from the waste management sector (ERP Portugal, LIPOR and Porto Ambiente), the technology and innovation sector (Porto Digital and UPTEC) and the university sector (Faculty of Engineering of the University of Porto, Higher Institute of Engineering of Porto, and Portucalense University). These partners worked together to recover computer equipment that is no longer in use by companies, organisations and individuals. Through a training programme and Repair Café events, participants gain the skills to diagnose and repair their own computers, as well as assisting with repairs on computers that are no longer in use, thus ensuring their continued availability to other users. Results in 2023 and 2024 revealed a total of 721 units of collected equipment, 3225.5 kg of collected equipment, 290 units of repaired equipment and 1371.6 kg of repaired weight. To expand this work, in 2024, the Center for Circularity of the City of Porto - ECOPORTO was created to promote reuse, giving a second life to objects that would otherwise end up in the trash, through the repair and donation of electrical and electronic equipment and furniture. The focus is on raising awareness and literacy around circularity and sustainability, with the aim of extending the life cycle and retaining the value of materials, encouraging behavior change among all who live in Porto. ReBOOT is now integrated in ECOPORTO. The EcoPorto results from September 2024 e to July 2025 reveals a total of 13064 kg of goods collected, with 5317 kg reused and donated.

column16: One of the first eFuel production units in Europe could be implemented in the Porto Region (at the Energy Recovery Plant of LIPOR). This project has the potential to transform the energy recovery of waste and decarbonise the aviation sector. A consortium comprising LIPOR, P2X Europe and Veolia Portugal is currently undertaking feasibility studies for the implementation of an industrial-scale Power-to-Liquid (PtL) unit. The project's objective is to produce a synthetic green fuel (eFuel) for the aviation industry from a combination of CO2 (carbon dioxide) captured from the plant's process and hydrogen from renewable energies. In the initial phase, approximately 100 thousand tons of captured biogenic CO2 will be recycled for conversion into eFuel, which will then be transformed into several renewable-based products, including eKerosene, eDiesel and specific chemical products.

Developing low-carbon mobility is one of the major climate change mitigation measures in Turku's Climate Plan. Under this plan, Turku is investing in redesigning its city center to make it more conducive to “soft mobility” (ie. human-powered, non-motorized mobility).

Turku's public transport equipment has already been widely converted to electric alternatives, an electric tram is under development.

The city has already started diversifying its low-emission mobility options with a city-bike and an electric scooter sharing system. 

As part of Smart and Wise Turku, one of the city's spearhead projects that combines the Smart City concept with the region's 2029 carbon neutrality goal, Turku has been working on ensuring city logistics are emission free. As the transport system is developed regionally, Turku´s resource-wise mobility system will also be strengthened by the implementation of the “Land Use, Housing and Transport Agreement” and the “Regional Structure Model 2035” together with neighboring municipalities and the regional council.

As part of the EU-funded 1.5-degree city project, city of Turku develops residents' opportunities to participate in climate work, supports companies' low-carbon business operations and creates a platform for monitoring emission reductions in the area. The development of the project utilises behavioural sciences and, in particular, a method called nudging, which makes climate-friendly choice a more attractive option for the user. This will be used to reduce emissions from commuting among other things.

The general objective of the Krakow transport policy is: Creation of conditions for efficient and safe movement of people and goods while limiting the harmful impact on the natural environment and living conditions of residents, and improving communication accessibility within the city, as well as areas of the metropolitan area, province and country in conditions of sustainable mobility in the urban transport system.Main objective I - Ensuring the possibility of convenient movement for users of the transport system in internal and external connectionsMain objective II - Development and promotion of ecological forms of travelMain Objective III - Improvement of the natural environment, reduction of transport nuisance for residents and increase of safetyMain objective IV - Improvement of the efficiency of spatial management and transportMain objective V - Improvement of the city's image and building its prestigeIn order to implement the assumed goals, it is necessary to take such actions as:- modernization and extension of the tram infrastructure,- replacement of the tram rolling stock with low-floor tram rolling stock, equipped with an audiovisual passenger information system,- introducing a bus fleet to service public transport lines: meeting the highest emission standards, hybrid and electric,- construction or separation of bus lanes on the most congested communication routes and gradual introduction of Bus Rapid Transit,- construction of new railway stops in the city as part of the Fast Agglomeration Railway (SKA) system,- construction of tunnel sections in the most sensitive areas, where the capacity of the collective transport system has been exhausted,- development of an area traffic control system for subsequent tram routes with an extension for bus transport,- development of bicycle infrastructure, including the connection with the public transport network,- creating a joint transport offer,- timetable coordination,- introduction of a common ticket for agglomeration travel by all means of public transport,- common passenger information,- construction of new and modernization of existing transfer nodes,- construction of P&R car parks mainly at railway stations and stops, in the vicinity of the 3rd and 4th ring roads outside the areas of concentration of housing and workplaces and access roads to them,The Transport Policy in many places takes into account the concept of SUMP (Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan) widely promoted by the European Commission, which is a new planning concept that responds in a more balanced and integrated way to challenges and problems related to transport in urban areas. The main goal of this approach is to create a sustainable transport system in Krakow by:- increasing the efficiency of passenger and cargo transport in the city,- providing all residents with access to jobs and services,- ensuring the comfort and safety of urban transport,- increasing the attractiveness and quality of the urban environment,- reducing environmental pollution, the greenhouse effect and the level of energy consumption by transporting passengers and cargo in the city.It is worth mentioning, that Krakow already started work on its SUMP (Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan). 

In 2023, the Krakow City Council passed a resolution adopting and implementing the SUMP - Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan.
 This document provides a coherent direction of actions in the field of sustainable mobility, striving to achieve the main goal of ensuring a sustainable and user-friendly transport system, taking into account the even development of all forms of mobility. It also organizes issues related to sustainable mobility in the municipalities covered by the plan.

La ordenanza 8757 de la ciudad de Rosario es fundamental al establecer normativas rigurosas sobre los aspectos higrotérmicos en la construcción. Al regular parámetros como el aislamiento térmico y la gestión de la humedad en los edificios, se garantiza un mayor confort para los habitantes y se optimiza el consumo energético. Esto es esencial para reducir la dependencia de sistemas artificiales de climatización, lo que disminuye el gasto energético y prolonga la vida útil de las edificaciones al prevenir daños por humedad y condensación.

Esta regulación cobra aún más relevancia en el contexto del cambio climático, ya que promueve prácticas de construcción sustentable y eficiente que contribuyen a la reducción de emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero. Al mejorar la eficiencia energética de las edificaciones, se disminuye la demanda de energía y, por ende, las emisiones asociadas a su generación. De esta manera, la ordenanza 8757 no solo mejora la calidad de vida de los ciudadanos de Rosario, sino que también representa un paso significativo hacia la mitigación del impacto ambiental y la promoción de un desarrollo urbano sostenible.
Actualmente ya se construyeron 1371 edificios que representan 2.552.161m2 que cumplen con la ordenanza.

column16: La ciudad impulsa una gestión integral de los residuos sólidos urbanos que comprende todas las etapas, desde la generación de los residuos hasta el tratamiento y la disposición final de los mismos, buscando tanto su optimización como la sustentabilidad ambiental, climática y económica. Desde 2004, Rosario ha avanzado hacia un Plan de Gestión Integral de Residuos Sólidos Urbanos (PGIRSU) con el objetivo de contar con un instrumento rector con sus objetivos y lineamientos, numerosos de sus proyectos se han puesto en marcha y otros se han ido modificando en el tiempo, en función de los requerimientos y necesidades surgidas. Se encuentra en concordancia con el Plan de Máxima a reducción a fin de minimizar el volumen de residuos. El PGIRSU tiene como fin minimizar los impactos negativos sobre la salud y el ambiente producidos por los residuos, desde su generación hasta su disposición final. Constituye la línea conductora de las intervenciones en un proceso dinámico, que se evalúa y ajusta a las circunstancias socioeconómicas vigentes, y que avanza bajo los principios de prevención, reducción, valorización, transparencia en la información, inclusión social, entre otros. Uno de los programas con mayor alcance y recorrido es el Programa SEPARE, que funciona desde 2009, y que a través de diferentes modalidades de servicios y estrategias ha instalado entre la población la importancia de la separación de residuos en diferentes fracciones, a fin de que sean posibles de procesos de valorización, reciclado o transformación biológica. Entre las modalidades que desarrolla el programa están: Servicio de recolección de residuos reciclables puerta a puerta, Centros de recepción en instituciones, islas de separación en vía pública, separación de papel en oficinas públicas, recolección de Aceite Vegetal Usado, recepción de aparatos informáticos, recepción de pilas usadas y baterías (estos últimos enmarcados en la recepción y tratamiento de residuos especiales), la gestión de neumáticos fuera de uso, entre otras actuaciones. También cuenta con la iniciativa de Barrios Verdes, que es una intervención focalizada en determinados barrios, donde se ha implementado un servicio de recolección de residuos domiciliarios organizado en tres fracciones distintas: orgánicos, reciclables y restos. En esta misma línea, la separación de residuos de los Grandes Generadores, la optimización de la recolección de los residuos verdes, la inclusión social de los recuperadores urbanos mejorando sus condiciones de trabajo y de vida, etc. Cabe señalar que la estrategia de reducción de desperdicios de alimentos se ha ido consolidando y en la actualidad, se gestiona junto al Banco de Alimentos de Rosario (BAR) y el Mercado de Productores con el fin de no desechar alimentos (frutas y verduras) y sean aprovechados por quienes lo necesitan, por lo cual son beneficiados más de 300 organismos con carácter social. Otra iniciativa que se desarrolla de forma periódica desde hace varios años para la revalorización de materiales, son jornadas de recepción de textiles para evitar que terminen en el relleno sanitario, y los elementos obtenidos son entregados a organizaciones sociales de la ciudad que trabajan con población en situación de calle. Se trabaja además, en la optimización y funcionamiento de la productividad y capacidad operativa de las estructuras que conforman el Centro Ambiental de Tratamiento de Residuos. Así como en el desarrollo de nuevas estructuras e instalaciones de equipamientos con diferentes tecnologías para el tratamiento y disposición final de los residuos que contribuyan a disminuir las emisiones de GEI, la producción de energía a partir de los residuos y a reducir al desperdicio de los recursos. 2.	社会公众参与低碳行动：引导社会公众参与公共交通出行、新能源汽车使用、节气节电、生活垃圾分类等降碳行动，逐步形成覆盖“衣、食、住、行、用”等方面的低碳生活方式。
3.	开发低碳场景：通过开发多元化的低碳场景，鼓励公众在日常生活中选择低碳产品和服务，减少高碳商品的消费。
4.	碳积分兑换机制：设计完善碳积分生成和兑换规则，推出碳积分兑换奖励等活动，吸引用户积极参与降碳行动，促进低碳消费。
5.	公益激励活动：策划开展植树造林、景区巡护、绿道骑行等主题活动，扩大碳普惠的社会影响力，鼓励公众参与绿色低碳行为。
6.	碳普惠商城：建设碳普惠商城，提供用于碳积分兑换的商品和服务，鼓励消费者选择低碳产品。

Categories for the amended code include: 1. Site Sustainability (Promoting open and green spaces, sustainable mobility, and urban heat reduction), 2. Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (Promoting passive design, efficient appliances, and renewable energy), 3. Water Efficiency and Wastewater Management (Promoting efficient fixtures, rainwater collection, and water reuse), 4. Material Sustainability and Solid Waste Management (Using of more sustainable materials and adoption of 5Rs strategy), and 5. Indoor Environmental Quality (Using passive design, ventilation, and lighting, and limiting use of toxic materials).

column16: 1.推行舊料再生永續：臺南為推廣舊建材循環使用之風氣，在文化部文化資產局的經費挹注下，2017年7月率全國之先成立「臺南市文化資產建材銀行」(https://law01.tainan.gov.tw/GLRSNEWSOUT/NewsContent.aspx?id=2178)。建材銀行是將古蹟、歷史建築修復案場、報廢拆除的公有房舍、私人捐贈等舊料，經過清潔整理，使舊料達到可被再使用的程度，逐步實踐舊料制度化收存管理與再利用之目標。本市透過建立全國首創的系統化管理機制、提高建材申請之再利用率及建材使用途徑之多元化、舊料再生教育及推廣、物料媒合再利用諮詢及輔導等策略以達成舊料循環深入各層級，並擴大推廣社會大眾「惜物」及「低碳環保」觀念。除引導舊材管理邁向全面制度化，同時積極向社會大眾或社區推廣，以建材再利用結合傳統技藝之創意加值，落實並提升文資保存觀念及水準。長期展望於2030年累計領出舊材15,000件。\n2.營建土石方再利用：現行出土與需土工程間之營建剩餘土石方互相利用者，稱為土方交換。公共工程於規劃設計中營建餘土如有剩餘或不足，可利用「營建剩餘土石方資訊服務中心」（https://www.soilmove.tw/）申報土方交換案件，搜尋適當土方交換對象。臺南市於2012年訂定「臺南市營建工程賸餘土石方處理及資源堆置處理場設置 管理自治條例 」，並於2017年、2023年修訂。其中營建剩餘土石方之種類，包括建築工程、公共工程、其他民間工程及收容處理場所產生之剩餘泥、土、砂、石、磚、瓦、混凝土塊等，經暫屯、堆置可供回收、分類、加工、轉運、處理、再生利用者，屬有用之土壤砂石資源。2020年土方產出量為1,817,089立方公尺，共交換908,988立方公尺土方，交換率達50%。2021年土方產出量為 2,046,150立方公尺，共交換510,693立方公尺土方，交換率達 25%。\n3.推動綠建築：依據《臺南市低碳城市自治條例》，本市公有或經本府公告指定地區之新建建築物，須取得綠建築標章，設置太陽能熱水設備、再生能源發電系統或屋頂綠化設施，以及採用雨水貯留回收系統。

column16: Malaysia has embarked a journey of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), where apart from reducing the consumption of traditional petroleum in aircraft, Malaysia is actively exploring its adaptation to SAF into its long-term aviation strategies. SAF emerges as a pivotal global term in the contemporary aviation industry and offers alternatives to decouple GHG emissions from flights. SAF comprised of renewable biomass and waste resources with potential to deliver the performance of petroleum-based jet fuel but with a fraction of its carbon footprint. As compared to the traditional jet fuel, SAF is expected to reduce up to 65% of carbon emissions, per the estimation provided by the International Air Transport Association. However, SAF is not a novel terminology in Malaysia as Malaysia Airlines has already flew its flight from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore using blended traditional jet fuel with SAF last year, in conjunction with World Environment Day. SAF are produced by Neste, the world's largest producer of SAF, while the product handling and refueling are managed by Petronas Dagangan Berhad (PDB) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). PDB is currently a supplier of SAF and it is expected to become a producer of SAF in the fourth quarter of this year. https://www.azmilaw.com/insights/sustainability-in-aviation-industry-malaysias-perspective/

In 2020, Low Carbon Calendar Competition was introduced which the component includes reduction of water consumption (m3), electricity (kWh) and also the amount of recycling (kg). One of the feedback received in 2020 was there is lack of facilities/ area for community to send their recyclable item. As such starting in 2021, the concept of drive thru events was introduced so community can easily access to a one stop centre for them to drop recycling item. The booth provided for the drive thru events included recyclable items such as paper, plastic, aluminum tin etc; also, a dedicated booth for used cooking oil collection. They can also drop their unwanted fabric and stationery and books for donation. The first drive thru event was held in Sutera Mall in April 2021, the two days event successfully collected 2875.00 kg of recyclable items which is equivalent in reducing 8252.69 kgCO2 of carbon emission. On 4th and 5th December, another drive thru was conducted at Sunway Big Box. Despite the event held at Iskandar Puteri, the event received the support from people of Segamat, Pontian, Kulai etc. The two days event successfully collected 1721.90 kg recyclable items which resulted in reducing 49441.85 kgCO2 of carbon emission. Three drive thru events conducted in 2022 with total collections of 42,139kg recycle items including fabric and oil. The concept of drive thru- dedicated area, events for community to drop recycle items has been replicated by other local authorities and private entities. In 2024, the total collection of fabric, 3R,and used cooking oil 79.694.57kg, total of water and electricity saved 16,345.76 kgCO2 equivalents. with overall total of carbon saved in 2024 380,723.13 KgCO2 equivalent.

Trees make Münster worth living in! As a source of shade and CO2 storage, they are an important part of Münster's green lungs. In addition, street trees in particular are already at their tolerance limit at many locations due to small tree discs, compacted soils and various pollutant inputs. Climate protection measures continue to be highly relevant - but are no longer sufficient on their own. It is necessary to find new, creative ways to develop Münster into a resilient city that is adapted to the consequences of climate change.

Non-plastic customer friendly stores in New Taipei City: Stores in New Taipei City that meet at least two of the following criteria, upon review, are recognized as environmentally conscious businesses:
--Do not provide any single-use items (e.g., chopsticks, plates, cups, straws) for dine-in customers.
--Encourage customers to bring their own reusable tableware or shopping bags.
--Use plastic-free or reusable materials for product packaging.
--Adopt eco-friendly containers for food delivery with a return and reuse system.
--Offer discounts to customers who bring their own containers or bags for take-out.
--Provide rental services for reusable cups or bags.
--Implement other innovative plastic reduction initiatives (e.g., point-based reward programs).
Eligible businesses will be awarded the “No-Plastic Guest” label to highlight their commitment to sustainability and plastic reduction.

It serves as one of 210 model sites promoting plastic reduction and circular economy. The store features the “i-Circle Smart Recycling Machine” for collecting PET bottles and batteries. Recycled PET bottles are remanufactured into products such as tote bags and reusable shopping bags, which are sold in-store. It also offers “OPEN iECO” reusable cup rental services.

Plastic-Free Markets: Since 2019, New Taipei City has promoted “Plastic-Free Markets,” reducing over 180,000 plastic bags to date. Starting May 1, 2025, all 41 public markets in the city have fully transitioned to plastic-free operations, with vendors no longer offering plastic shopping bags by default. To support this effort, secondhand bag collection boxes (“reBAG Sharing Stations”) are available on-site for public use. The initiative is expected to eliminate 300,000 single-use plastic bags annually.

https://www.klimahelsingor.dk/ - The 'Plan for Klima og Bæredygtighed 2020-2030' outlines several initiatives to minimize emissions in the transport sector. Key measures include: 1. **Electrification of Vehicles**: The plan emphasizes the gradual replacement of the municipal vehicle fleet with electric vehicles. By 2030, at least 50% of the fleet is expected to be low-emission vehicles. 2. **Reduction of Emissions from Heavy Vehicles**: The municipality will develop a plan to reduce CO2 emissions from heavy vehicles, such as buses and trucks, by prioritizing the use of biofuels or hydrogen when electric alternatives are not viable. 3. **Promoting Cycling and Reducing Transport Needs**: The plan promotes cycling among municipal employees by providing electric and regular bicycles and running awareness campaigns. Additionally, infrastructure improvements, such as installing charging stations at municipal workplaces, will support this transition. 4. **Compensatory Measures**: For unavoidable emissions, such as those from necessary air travel, compensatory actions like afforestation or wetland restoration are encouraged. 


Plan 2: The cycling plan 
https://helsingor.dk/Media/638373816282537972/cyklistplan-2020-2030-inkl-indsatskatalog.pdf
Since 2010, Helsingør Municipality has pursued an active effort to promote cycling.
The Cycling Plan sets the direction for political prioritization of cycling initiatives and projects and also guides the administration's work in promoting cycling.

The overall goal of the plan is:
'The overarching goal of the cycling effort in Helsingør Municipality with this plan is to get more people to choose the bicycle as their primary mode of transport by 2030.'

The plan includes four specific objectives: 1) Improve accessibility, 2) Reduce the number of injured cyclists, 3) Encourage more children and young people to choose active transportation to and from school and institutions, 4) Encourage more people to combine cycling with public transportation

The plan does not have a direct goal of reducing CO₂ emissions but contributes indirectly to the broader effort to promote sustainable living.

1. Diagnóstico del sitio
Evaluación de las condiciones actuales del lugar (ubicación, capacidad, infraestructura, vida útil).
Identificación de impactos ambientales existentes: lixiviados, gases, fauna nociva, incendios, contaminación de suelos y aguas.
Cumplimiento con la normatividad (NOM-083-SEMARNAT-2003 sobre sitios de disposición final).

2. Acciones técnicas para la regularización
Control de lixiviados: construcción o mejora de sistemas de captación y tratamiento.
Manejo de biogás: instalación de chimeneas de venteo o sistemas de aprovechamiento energético.
Compactación y cobertura de residuos: uso de maquinaria y cobertura diaria con material inerte para evitar fauna nociva y malos olores.
Mejoras de infraestructura: accesos, cercado, báscula, caseta de control.
Plan de cierre y/o ampliación: en caso de que el sitio esté por agotar su vida útil.

3. Cumplimiento legal y administrativo
Elaboración y registro del Programa de Regularización ante la autoridad ambiental (SEMARNAT/SEMADET).
Trámite de autorizaciones de impacto ambiental y de vida útil.
Establecimiento de bitácoras de operación y monitoreo ambiental.
Capacitación del personal encargado del manejo de residuos.

4. Acciones complementarias
Campañas de separación y valorización de residuos para reducir la cantidad que llega al sitio.
Proyectos de aprovechamiento de materiales reciclables y orgánicos (composta, lombricomposta, reciclaje).
Medidas de seguridad laboral para el personal y formalización de pepenadores.

La Ordenanza de Edificaciones de San Borja es un marco normativo que regula la construcción, remodelación y uso de edificaciones en el distrito, con el objetivo de garantizar la seguridad, sostenibilidad y calidad urbana. Esta ordenanza establece criterios técnicos y ambientales que deben cumplir todas las obras, promoviendo un desarrollo ordenado y respetuoso con el entorno.

Entre los aspectos más relevantes, la ordenanza incorpora normas para la eficiencia energética, fomentando el uso de materiales ecoamigables y tecnologías que reduzcan el consumo de energía y agua. Asimismo, promueve la inclusión de áreas verdes y espacios públicos accesibles en los proyectos arquitectónicos, contribuyendo a mejorar la calidad de vida y la resiliencia urbana frente al cambio climático.

La normativa también regula la altura, densidad y diseño de las construcciones, buscando mantener la armonía con el paisaje urbano y evitar la saturación de servicios e infraestructura. Se contemplan medidas para la gestión de residuos durante la construcción y para minimizar impactos ambientales.

Además, la ordenanza incluye disposiciones para garantizar la seguridad estructural y accesibilidad universal, facilitando la movilidad de personas con discapacidad. En conjunto, estas normas buscan que las edificaciones en San Borja sean sostenibles, seguras y estén alineadas con los objetivos de desarrollo urbano sostenible del distrito.

El programa “San Borja en Bici” es una iniciativa pionera en el Perú, implementada por la Municipalidad de San Borja con el objetivo de promover el uso de la bicicleta como medio de transporte sostenible, saludable y no contaminante. Este programa forma parte de la estrategia del distrito para mitigar los efectos del cambio climático, reducir las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero y fomentar una cultura de movilidad responsable.

San Borja fue el primer distrito en Lima en implementar una red de ciclovías integradas, que actualmente superan los 30 km de extensión, conectando parques, avenidas principales y estaciones del sistema de bicicletas públicas. Estas ciclovías están diseñadas con criterios de seguridad vial y accesibilidad.

El programa incluye el préstamo gratuito de bicicletas en estaciones distribuidas estratégicamente por el distrito, promoviendo su uso en actividades cotidianas como ir al trabajo, al colegio o realizar trámites. También se desarrollan campañas educativas y actividades comunitarias para fomentar el respeto entre ciclistas, peatones y conductores.

“San Borja en Bici” ha sido reconocido como modelo de movilidad sostenible urbana y ha servido de inspiración para otros distritos. Esta política pública reafirma el compromiso de San Borja con un desarrollo urbano más limpio, seguro y amigable con el medio ambiente.

La gestión de residuos sólidos en San Borja se basa en un enfoque integral que combina infraestructura moderna, educación ambiental y políticas públicas orientadas a la sostenibilidad. La municipalidad ha instalado modernos contenedores subterráneos en 50 puntos estratégicos del distrito, lo que mejora la disposición de los residuos, la limpieza urbana y facilita el trabajo del personal encargado de la recolección. Además, se han implementado “islas ecológicas inteligentes” equipadas con sensores que permiten la segregación adecuada de materiales reciclables y notifican cuando están llenas, incentivando la participación ciudadana en el reciclaje.

San Borja también realiza campañas de sensibilización y talleres para educar a la población sobre la importancia de separar los residuos en origen y promover el reciclaje. Estas acciones buscan fortalecer la cultura ambiental y la corresponsabilidad ciudadana en la gestión de residuos.

En reconocimiento a sus buenas prácticas, la municipalidad recibió el “Distintivo Recicla 2024” por su gestión responsable de residuos electrónicos (RAEE), siendo el único distrito de Lima Metropolitana en obtenerlo. Asimismo, se aprobó un estudio técnico para mejorar la gestión de residuos sólidos municipales, evidenciando el compromiso del distrito con una gestión eficiente, sostenible y participativa.
